Release title 
Fauna Hunt 2.1.1 - direction arrows, and a character fix
Release notes 
## New: direction arrows

Every contact now has a small arrow beside it, pointing where the animal is relative to your nose. Straight up means dead ahead.

The arrow is deliberately **no more precise than the words next to it** — it snaps to the same steps the text uses, so it gives nothing away that you were not already being told. It is just far quicker to read at a glance, especially in VR.

## Fixed

* **Damaged characters.** In 2.1.0 bearings read `070Â°` instead of `070°`, and several dashes were destroyed. Anyone running 2.1.0 should replace it.

## The helper app is gone (since 2.1.0)

Fauna Hunt used to need a second program running alongside the simulator. It was the source of every awkward thing about installing this: a black window you had to leave open, a SmartScreen warning, antivirus flagging an unsigned executable, and a 20 MB download mostly made of bundled Python.

**All of that is gone.** The work happens inside the simulator itself. Copy one folder into Community, start the sim, done.

## If you were testing 1.2.x

* **Delete the old folder first**, then copy the new one in. Do not merge them.
* **Stop using `FaunaHuntService.exe`** — it no longer exists and is not needed.
* **Your score and lifelist are kept.** They live in the simulator's own save data.

## Also in this line

* **VR: you can identify from any direction.** The simulator will not tell add-ons where a headset is aimed, so rather than make you point the aircraft at an animal, that check is off in VR. In a 2D cockpit view it works as before.
* **Settings shows the version**, so it is obvious which build is running.

## Known limitations

* **No birds.** The simulator keeps its flying animals somewhere add-ons cannot reach. Ground animals only.
* **MSFS 2024 only.** The animal data does not exist in 2020.

## Install

1. Download `FaunaHunt-v2.1.1.zip` below.
2. Copy the `wilem35-fauna-hunt` folder into your Community folder.
3. Start MSFS 2024 and click the paw print in the toolbar.

Good places to hunt: HTSN Seronera (Serengeti), HKAM Amboseli, FASZ Skukuza. Turn up the simulator's own **Fauna** graphics setting for more to find — it is set separately for normal and VR.

03 flightsim.to

Upload the same zip. Each block below matches a box on the form.

Title 
Fauna Hunt - Wildlife Spotting Game
Short description 
There is wildlife all over Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 and you have been flying straight over it. Fauna Hunt is a hunting game - track them down, work out what you are looking at, and get close enough for the shot.
Description 
There is wildlife all over Flight Simulator 2024, and you have been flying straight over it for years. Elephants, wildebeest, camels, bison, kangaroos, snow leopards. Fauna Hunt makes finding them the reason for the flight.


THE HUNT

A spotter calls contacts over the intercom, and he is not very helpful.

   something very large, on its own - bearing 230 - 1100 m

Fly out that way and he gets more specific.

   15 animals - your 7 o'clock, low - 900 m

That is as much as you get. He never tells you what they are. Getting close enough to see for yourself is the whole game.


IDENTIFY IT

Once you can see the animals, tap the contact. You get four species to choose from - and that is where it gets interesting, because a Grant's gazelle and a Thomson's gazelle look an awful lot alike at 400 metres in a helicopter that will not sit still.

Get it right and the animal joins your collection. First guess is worth the most, so it pays to have a proper look before you commit.


THEN GO AND GET THE SHOT

Identifying it is only half of it. Fly within 150 metres of the herd and you capture it, for the points all over again. This is the part that puts you down on the deck, low and slow, drifting over a river full of hippos - which is where this simulator is at its absolute best anyway.


61 ANIMALS TO FIND

From cattle and sheep in the local fields, up to seven legendary animals that live in only a handful of places on Earth. Snow leopards. Giant pandas. Orcas. Rarer animals are worth far more, and you get a heads-up when a legendary one is close.

Plenty of them have subspecies to sort out too - there are eight different giraffes and seven different brown bears out there, and they all count separately.


THE LIFELIST

Your lifelist keeps track of everything you have caught. The ones you are still missing tell you where to go looking - "Himalaya: Ladakh, Nepal, Bhutan, Tibet" - which is how a quiet evening turns into planning a trip to Mongolia to find a wild horse.

Most of the good stuff is African. A bush flight across the Serengeti is worth a hundred laps of the local farmland.


DIFFICULTY

Three settings that change how much the spotter gives away and how early:

   Explorer - detail arrives early. Good for learning what a distant giraffe actually looks like.

   Tracker - the intended balance.

   Expert - you stay in the dark until you are nearly on top of it, and everything scores 50% more.


INSTALLATION

Drop the wilem35-fauna-hunt folder into your Community folder and start the simulator. Click the paw print in the toolbar.

Where to start: HTSN Seronera in the Serengeti, HKAM Amboseli, or FASZ Skukuza in Kruger. Anywhere with farmland will give you cattle and horses to practise on.

One tip: the simulator has its own Fauna slider in its graphics settings. Turn it up and there is a great deal more to hunt. It is set separately for normal and VR, so check both.


GOOD TO KNOW

No birds. The simulator keeps its flying animals somewhere add-ons cannot reach. Ground animals only.

In VR you can identify from any direction. The simulator will not tell add-ons where your head is pointing, so rather than make you aim the aircraft at a zebra, that check is off in VR.
